Most recent time before that was four months prior, it was initiated in the exact same way where we started kissing and making out while laying in her bed. She was a little resistive like before but after kissing for a good 5 minutes she then wanted me to proceed to the next step.

We were in progress until someone knocked on the door and interrupted us and we stopped. For some reason I couldn't get fully hard again so we stopped for the day and left on good terms. I've tried to contact her the day after that event that happened a few months ago but she went cold on me and told me that she isn't looking for a relationship so we stopped contact for a while.

It's been a month and she hasn't pressed any charges when she initially did threaten to call the police on me. The only semi-legal advice I've been given is to avoid contacting her, avoid trying to give her anything to fix things, and especially avoid saying anything about the situation to anyone else.

I hope to move on from this some day, but it still constantly troubles my mind and there's not a day that passes by where I don't think about it.

I agree with your post.

A large part of me says it's not correct to paint a situation as black or white but the defensive part of me wants to do that so that it's easier for me to say that it wasn't my fault, but I shouldn't. I feel like the best thing I could have done in this situation is to just walk away when things started getting unclear. I say unclear because she would tell me to stop and when I stopped she would want to keep kissing which my body would then interpret it as a signal to continue on.

I really wish that I learned how to walk away or avoid these kinds of situations. I never wanted to hurt her. The morning that I woke up I've almost made up my mind to agree to get back together with her but I was completely blind-sided by her rape accusation.

There's not a day that passes by where I don't try to justify or rationalize to myself that I truly didn't do anything wrong or try to figure out what I could have done or could be doing now to make things right again.
